nodes.title: Perfect stable categories and localizing invariants
nodes.statement: Cat∞perf has small idempotent-complete stable ∞-categories as objects and exact functors as morphisms. A sequence C→D→E is exact when its composite is zero, C→D is fully faithful, and Idem(D/C)→E is an equivalence. A weakly localizing invariant with values in a stable ∞-category V is a functor F:Cat∞perf→V with F(0)=0 carrying these sequences to fiber/cofiber sequences. No continuity is included in this definition; accessible/finitary refinements remain RT.5’s responsibility.
hypotheses: C,D,E are small stable idempotent-complete ∞-categories; V is stable.
Exact sequences include a specified zero composite.
Universe bounds are fixed explicitly; changing universe uses the specified enlargement comparisons.
proofSteps: Use the existing stable ∞-category, Verdier quotient and idempotent-completion interfaces from EDS.
Define exact sequences by the quotient universal property and formulate localizing invariants as a full subcategory of functors.
Compare exactness with the induced compactly generated presentable localization after Ind; split sequences give biproducts.
acceptance: The sequence C→C→0 is exact and F(C)→F(C)→0 is a fiber sequence.

nodes.title: The stable S-construction
nodes.statement: For a small stable ∞-category C, let S_r(C) be its ∞-category of gap diagrams on Ar([r]): diagonal entries are zero and every subinterval square is a pushout. For r≥1 restriction identifies S_r(C)≃Fun([r−1],C), but its simplicial faces are the gap-diagram faces, including quotient faces. Iterated core realization and looping define Kconn(C); additivity gives Kconn(C)≃Ω|Kconn(S•C)|. Construct the comparison with the parent’s Waldhausen S-construction on a presenting Waldhausen category.
hypotheses: C is small stable; its presenting Waldhausen model admits the required homotopy pushouts and weak-equivalence comparison.
r≥1 is required for the chain equivalence.
Universe bounds are fixed explicitly; changing universe uses the specified enlargement comparisons.
proofSteps: Construct interval diagrams with their quotient objects by finite colimits.
Use restriction to increasing chains to identify each positive simplicial degree; derive the faces from restriction of interval diagrams.
Transport Waldhausen additivity and delooping through the enhancement comparison, using the spectrum assembly supplied by H.5:S-delooping.

nodes.title: Nonconnective K-theory of stable categories
nodes.statement: Construct Knc:Cat∞perf→Sp by flasque enlargement and suspension: for a sufficiently large uncountable regular κ set FκC=(Ind_ω C)^κ, the κ-compact objects in the ordinary filtered Ind-completion, and set ΣκC=Idem(FκC/C). Define Knc(C) as the colimit of Ω^rKconn(Σκ^rC). Prove independence of the permitted κ, τ≥0Knc(C)≃Kconn(C), equivalence invariance and filtered-colimit preservation. For ordinary exact/Frobenius models compare with Bass–Schlichting K-theory. Knc is weakly localizing; connective K need not send every exact sequence to a fiber sequence.
hypotheses: C is small stable idempotent-complete; κ is sufficiently large uncountable regular for the chosen universe.
Universe bounds are fixed explicitly; changing universe uses the specified enlargement comparisons.
proofSteps: The κ-compact subcategory FκC contains countable coproducts because κ is uncountable regular; use their exact countable-sum swindle to make its connective K-theory zero.
Form the stable quotient FκC/C and its idempotent completion in Cat∞perf, then iterate the suspension comparison maps.
Check change of universe/κ using cofinal enlargement comparisons; prove localization by the quotient diagram and the parent’s fibration theorem.
Compare the enhancement of Frobenius pairs at each suspension stage, not just homotopy groups in nonnegative degrees.
acceptance: A flasque stable category has zero Knc, and the suspension quotient deloops it in all integer degrees.

Consequently K(ker(q)^ω)→K(D^ω)→K(E^ω) is a fiber sequence.

Its kernel is generated by objects compact in the source.

Identify its compact objects as retracts of images of compacts of D.

nodes.title: The Land–Tamme replacement algebra
nodes.statement: For a homotopy pullback square of E1-rings A→B, A→A′, B→B′, A′→B′, construct C=A′⊙_A^{B′}B together with the canonical square A′→C, B→C. Its underlying spectrum is A′⊗_A B with the multiplication determined by the square, and C→B′ is the canonical multiplication map on that spectrum. Every weakly localizing invariant sends the square A→B, A′→C to a pullback square. No ordinary tensor-product E1-algebra structure on A′⊗_A B is assumed.
hypotheses: The input square is a homotopy pullback of E1-rings; connectivity is not required for the general formula.
The invariant is weakly localizing.
Universe bounds are fixed explicitly; changing universe uses the specified enlargement comparisons.
proofSteps: Form the lax pullback of perfect module categories and its full subcategory of glued objects.
Take the stable quotient, identify a compact generator, and define C by its endomorphism E1-algebra.
Compute its underlying bimodule as A′⊗_A B; the exact sequences and additivity identify the invariant square.
acceptance: If A′⊗_A B→B′ is an equivalence, every such invariant carries the original square to a pullback.

nodes.title: Truncating invariants on acyclic rings
nodes.statement: For a spectrum M and weakly localizing F:Cat∞perf→V, say F is truncating on M-acyclic connective rings if F(R)→F(Hπ0R) is an equivalence for every connective E1-ring R with M⊗R=0. Globally truncating means this for all connective R. Use the induced module action of R to check that its ring Postnikov truncations remain M-acyclic. The definition includes no hypothesis that F commutes with limits or filtered colimits.
hypotheses: F is weakly localizing; M is a spectrum; the rings in the predicate are connective and unital.
Universe bounds are fixed explicitly; changing universe uses the specified enlargement comparisons.
proofSteps: Define the restricted predicate using the concrete truncation ring map.
Prove that M-acyclicity of a unital R forces acyclicity of every R-module, in particular Hπ0R and τ≤kR.
Separate the restricted and global predicates so that global excision is applied only after checking its ring inputs.

nodes.title: Excision and nilinvariance for truncating invariants
nodes.statement: A globally truncating weakly localizing invariant is invariant under quotienting a discrete ring by a nilpotent ideal, and sends every Milnor square of discrete rings with a surjective side to a cartesian square. More generally apply the replacement-algebra theorem to connective ring pullbacks for which π0(A′)⊗_{π0A}π0(B)→π0(B′) is an isomorphism. The same proof applies to restricted truncation when every auxiliary connective replacement ring lies in the acyclic domain.
hypotheses: F is globally truncating, or all auxiliary rings have been proved to belong to its restricted acyclic domain.
The Milnor square is discrete with a surjective side.
Universe bounds are fixed explicitly; changing universe uses the specified enlargement comparisons.
proofSteps: Use the replacement-algebra theorem and compare π0C with π0B′ under the displayed tensor condition.
Replace C and B′ by their discrete π0 rings under F.
Deduce nilinvariance via the cone-ring pullback associated to a nilpotent ideal, as in Land–Tamme Corollary 3.5; verify closure of each restricted domain separately.
acceptance: An ordinary Milnor square with a surjective map is an instance, while an arbitrary square of connective rings is not.

nodes.title: Rational and p-adic truncation
nodes.statement: Let Λ be a localization of Z or Z/m for an integer m≥2. If f:A→B is a map of connective E1-rings inducing an isomorphism on π0, and Λ⊗f is n-connective for n≥1, then Λ⊗K(f) is (n+1)-connective. Here tensor with Z/m means Moore coefficients, and Λ-connectivity is measured on the coefficient fiber. In particular a Q- or Z/p-homology equivalence f with π0f an isomorphism induces the same equivalence on K. Thus K(R)→K(Hπ0R) is a rational equivalence for rationally discrete R, and a p-adic equivalence whenever R→Hπ0R is one; this includes every connective Z[1/p]-algebra ring spectrum.
hypotheses: A→B is connective E1 and induces a π0-isomorphism.
Λ is any localization of Z or Z/m for m≥2; the quantitative version requires n≥1. The rational and mod-p equivalence consequences take Λ=Q and Z/p respectively.
Universe bounds are fixed explicitly; changing universe uses the specified enlargement comparisons.
proofSteps: Control matrix ring and general-linear relative homology by the map A→B.
Use plus invariance of homology and the Serre-class relative Hurewicz/Whitehead argument.
Apply the quantitative statement to all finite connectivity levels to obtain rational and mod-p equivalences; retain π0-isomorphism throughout.
acceptance: For S[1/p]→HZ[1/p], K(S[1/p])→K(Z[1/p]) is a p-adic equivalence.

sources.match: Provides the homology-connectivity form of Waldhausen truncation.
Applies p-adic truncation after inverting p.

nodes.title: Nonpositive K-theory of connective rings
nodes.statement: For every connective E1-ring R, the map K_j(R)→K_j(π0R) is an isomorphism for all j≤0, naturally in ring maps. The parent’s Bass–Schlichting comparison identifies the target with its ordinary nonconnective ring K-theory. No nilpotent K0 theorem is assumed in this foundational comparison.
hypotheses: R is connective E1 and j≤0.
Universe bounds are fixed explicitly; changing universe uses the specified enlargement comparisons.
proofSteps: Identify K0 of perfect modules using connective projective retract presentations.
Compare the flasque enlargement and suspension used to construct negative K, as in BGT Theorem 9.53.
Use the parent’s comparison on ordinary rings to retain its existing Bass–Schlichting normalization.
acceptance: For connective R with π0R=Z, K0(R)=Z and all negative K groups vanish.

nodes.title: Bounded t-structures on stable ∞-categories
nodes.statement: A t-structure on a small stable ∞-category C is a t-structure on hC with full subcategories C≥0,C≤0 lifted to C; orthogonality and truncation triangles enhance to the truncation adjunctions. It is bounded if every object lies in C≥a∩C≤b for some integers a≤b depending on the object. The heart C♥=C≥0∩C≤0 is an ordinary abelian category. Reuse CategoryTheory.Triangulated.TStructure and its bounded object predicate on hC, with an explicit conversion from Mathlib’s cohomological shift to the homological spectral convention.
hypotheses: C is small stable with the imported triangulated structure on hC.
Bounds are allowed to depend on the object.
Universe bounds are fixed explicitly; changing universe uses the specified enlargement comparisons.
proofSteps: Lift the two full subcategories along C→hC and recover the enhanced truncation adjoints from mapping-space orthogonality.
Use the stable/triangulated shift comparison from E0 to fix the index signs.
Identify the heart’s mapping spaces as discrete and compare its kernels/cokernels with truncations of fibers/cofibers.
acceptance: Perf(Hk), for a field k, has the bounded standard t-structure with heart finite-dimensional k-vector spaces.

nodes.title: Stable envelopes and additive nonconnective K-theory
nodes.statement: For a small idempotent-complete additive ∞-category C, put Stab(C)=Funadd(Cop,Sp)^ω, the thick closure of the additive spectral Yoneda objects. This is the idempotent-complete stable envelope. An additive functor from C into a stable idempotent-complete category extends uniquely to an exact functor from Stab(C). Define Kadd,nc(C)=Knc(Stab(C)); prove τ≥0Kadd,nc(C)≃Kadd(C). For stable C, Yoneda uses the connective hom spectrum before stable extension; Stab(C) is not identified with C merely because C is already stable.
hypotheses: C is small idempotent-complete additive; the extension target is stable and idempotent-complete.
Universe bounds are fixed explicitly; changing universe uses the specified enlargement comparisons.
proofSteps: Use additive spectrum-valued presheaves and enriched Yoneda; the representables are compact generators.
Take their finite stable retract closure and prove the extension universal property.

Apply Hebestreit–Steimle’s group-completion theorem to the finite stable envelope. The assumed idempotent completeness of C makes its bounded weight heart idempotent-complete and hence its stable envelope idempotent-complete; justify this before identifying the thick envelope. Do not invoke invariance of connective K0 under arbitrary idempotent completion.
acceptance: For C=Projω(A) with A connective, Stab(C)≃Perf(A), so Kadd,nc(C)≃K(A).

nodes.title: The theorem of the heart and noetherian extension
nodes.statement: If C is small stable with a bounded t-structure, inclusion of the heart gives Kconn(C♥)≃Kconn(C), naturally for t-exact functors. If the heart is additionally noetherian, the same inclusion gives Knc(C♥)≃Knc(C). The latter extra hypothesis is retained; a general bounded heart is not used to assert a full nonconnective equivalence.
hypotheses: The t-structure is bounded.
The full nonconnective comparison additionally requires a noetherian heart.
Universe bounds are fixed explicitly; changing universe uses the specified enlargement comparisons.
proofSteps: Give the connective aisle its maximal Waldhausen structure and use truncation to compare its K-theory to C.
Apply the fibration/additivity argument to the acyclic truncation subcategory, then use the opposite category to isolate the heart.
For noetherian hearts apply AGH’s negative-K induction and vanishing argument before promoting the connective comparison to all degrees.
acceptance: For k a field, K(Perf(Hk))≃K(finite-dimensional k-vector spaces); boundedness alone gives only the connective comparison used later.

nodes.title: Regular ring-spectrum devissage
nodes.statement: Let R be connective, with π0R right regular noetherian and each πnR finitely generated as a right π0R-module. Here right regular for π0R means that every finitely generated right module has finite projective dimension. Assume every R-module M with ⊕nπnM finitely presented over π0R is perfect. Let R→S induce a localization Mod_R→Mod_S whose kernel is generated by a compact object (equivalently a finite set of compact objects). Suppose a perfect M is killed by extension to S exactly when ⊕nπnM is finitely presented over π0R. Then K(π0R)→K(R)→K(S) is a fiber sequence. The first map uses restriction from discrete π0R-modules, resolution and devissage; it is not generally extension along a ring map π0R→R.
hypotheses: π0R is right regular noetherian; every πnR is finitely generated over π0R; R is connective.
Every bounded R-module whose homotopy groups are finitely presented over π0R is perfect.
Extension Mod_R→Mod_S is a localization with kernel generated by finitely many compact objects.
A perfect module is in that kernel if and only if its total graded homotopy is finitely presented over π0R.
Universe bounds are fixed explicitly; changing universe uses the specified enlargement comparisons.
proofSteps: Use compact generation of the localization kernel to identify its compact objects with the bounded coherent R-modules. The finiteness of πnR and right noetherian π0R ensure that the standard truncations stay coherent.

Its standard t-structure is bounded with noetherian heart the finitely presented π0R-modules. Right regularity of π0R identifies the heart’s G-theory with projective K(π0R); apply the noetherian theorem of the heart.
Apply the nonconnective localization fiber sequence.
acceptance: If π*R=π0R[u] with u positive even and π0R regular noetherian, inverting u gives this fiber sequence; verify these conditions before using the example.

sources.locator: §4.2 definitions and Proposition 4.4, manuscript p.34; Example 4.6, p.35

nodes.title: Finite-limit control of the stable envelope
nodes.statement: For a small additive ∞-category C with finite limits, its perfect prestable additive-presheaf envelope A∞ω(C) is closed under finite limits inside additive presheaves of spaces. In the bounded-heart kernel of Stab(C)→C for C stable, the standard presheaf t-structure restricts to the kernel and every object has finite amplitude. This is the finite-limit input; closure under finite colimits alone would not establish restriction of truncations.
hypotheses: C is small additive with finite limits; the kernel application uses stable C.
Universe bounds are fixed explicitly; changing universe uses the specified enlargement comparisons.
proofSteps: Use the finite-presentation description of discrete additive presheaves as cokernels of maps of representables.
Apply the finite-limit argument to iterated loops and perfect presheaf presentations; use the representability criterion after sufficiently many loops.
Apply this prestable finite-limit closure to the stable finite-cell envelope and to the kernel generators coming from cofiber relations.
acceptance: The claim is used only for stable C, which has all finite limits; no claim is made for an arbitrary additive C lacking them.

Uses that theorem to restrict the t-structure to the relation kernel.

nodes.title: Levy’s bounded-heart fiber
nodes.statement: For every small idempotent-complete stable C, the exact extension Stab(C)→C is a localization with kernel D, and K(D)→Kadd,nc(C)→K(C) is a fiber sequence. The kernel D has a bounded t-structure, with no noetherian-heart assumption. This is the categorical construction underlying Levy’s alternative proof; its chromatic corollaries are separate targets in KII.10.
hypotheses: C is small stable idempotent-complete.
Universe bounds are fixed explicitly; changing universe uses the specified enlargement comparisons.
proofSteps: Extend id_C additively from the stable envelope and identify Funex(Cop,Sp)≃Ind(C) as its localization.
Generate its kernel by cofibers of the maps cofib(yA→yB)→yC for cofiber sequences A→B→C in C; these relation objects lie in the heart.
Use finite-limit control to restrict the presheaf t-structure, then finite generation by heart objects to obtain boundedness.
Apply nonconnective localization to the kernel; use the connective theorem of the heart only when the later chromatic corollary is proved.
acceptance: The kernel is generated by the specified cofiber-relation objects, not by arbitrary objects of Stab(C). A bounded heart does not by itself imply a full nonconnective heart comparison.

sources.match: Constructs the fiber and proves both chromatic conclusions using bounded t-structures.

nodes.title: Highly connective chromatic invariance
nodes.statement: For each n≥1 there is a bound N(n) such that an N(n)-connective map A→B of connective E1-rings that is an L_n^{p,f}-equivalence induces an L_n^{p,f}-equivalence K(A)→K(B). One may choose N=m−1 from the chromatic fiberwise-detection bound used in LMMT Proposition 3.1. Connectivity is a property of the underlying fiber spectrum.
hypotheses: n≥1; the ring map is connective E1, N(n)-connective and an L_n^{p,f}-equivalence.
Universe bounds are fixed explicitly; changing universe uses the specified enlargement comparisons.
proofSteps: Pass from A→B to the matrix and stabilized general-linear comparison, retaining the connectivity bound.
Use generalized fiberwise Serre detection to preserve the finite-localization equivalence on classifying spaces.
Use Bousfield–Kuhn to detect positive telescopic equivalences through plus; treat the T0 part by rational truncation.
acceptance: The bound is uniform over ring maps at fixed n; the theorem does not claim every connective equivalence on telescopes already has this property.

sources.match: Proves highly connective invariance using the §2 chromatic bounds.

nodes.title: Connectivity of the replacement algebra
nodes.statement: In a homotopy pullback square of E1-rings A→B, A→A′, B→B′, A′→B′ with A connective, suppose both vertical maps are n-connective and both horizontal maps are m-connective, with m,n≥0. Then A′⊙_A^{B′}B→B′ is (m+n+2)-connective. The estimate concerns this comparison map, not a purported ordinary algebra tensor product.
hypotheses: The square is a homotopy pullback; A is connective and m,n≥0.
Both parallel vertical maps are n-connective and both horizontal maps m-connective.
Universe bounds are fixed explicitly; changing universe uses the specified enlargement comparisons.
proofSteps: Write I=fib(A→A′) and J=fib(A→B), which are connective A-bimodules in the indicated degrees.
Identify the comparison fiber as Σfib(I⊗_A B→I), using the pullback square and its canonical splitting.
Use the cofiber sequence for A→B and the connective tensor-product estimate to obtain the sum of the connectivity bounds.
acceptance: If one side is an equivalence, the comparison is an equivalence; the finite estimate specializes accordingly.

sources.match: Computes the comparison fiber and the connectivity estimate.

nodes.title: One finite Postnikov stage suffices
nodes.statement: Let F be weakly localizing and M a spectrum. If there is a fixed k≥0 such that F(R)→F(τ≤kR) is an equivalence for every connective M-acyclic E1-ring R, then F is truncating on all such rings: F(R)→F(Hπ0R) is an equivalence. This uses a uniform finite k; it is not an interchange of F with an infinite Postnikov limit.
hypotheses: F is weakly localizing; k≥0 is uniform over all connective M-acyclic E1-rings.
Universe bounds are fixed explicitly; changing universe uses the specified enlargement comparisons.
proofSteps: For k>0 use the square-zero extension description of the kth Postnikov step as a pullback.
Apply the replacement-algebra invariant pullback square and its connectivity estimate to reduce the required cutoff.
Iterate the finite reduction to k=0, checking M-acyclicity of the auxiliary unital rings through their module structures.
acceptance: For k=0 the conclusion is precisely the assumption; the induction never assumes continuity of F.

sources.match: Reduces a uniform finite Postnikov comparison to truncation.

nodes.title: Telescopic K is truncating on finite-acyclic rings
nodes.statement: For n≥1 the invariant L_T(n)K is truncating on connective L_n^{p,f}-acyclic E1-rings. In particular, if R is such a ring, L_T(n)K(R)≃L_T(n)K(π0R).
hypotheses: n≥1; R is connective E1 and L_n^{p,f}-acyclic.
Universe bounds are fixed explicitly; changing universe uses the specified enlargement comparisons.
proofSteps: Choose the uniform bound in highly connective invariance.
For L_n^{p,f}-acyclic R, the map to that Postnikov stage has acyclic source and target and meets the connectivity bound.
Apply the finite-stage-to-truncating lemma to F=L_T(n)K.
acceptance: For n=1 this is only restricted truncation; the eventual statement for all K(1)-acyclic rings requires the height-one comparison and purity.

sources.match: Combines Proposition 3.1 with the Postnikov reduction.

nodes.title: Finite p-power coefficient vanishing
nodes.statement: For every r≥1 and i≥1, L_T(i)K(Z/p^r)=0. More generally L_T(i)K(A)=0 for a discrete Z/p^r-algebra A whenever i≤n and the acyclic-truncation/nilinvariance argument is applied in the L_n^{p,f}-acyclic setting used by Proposition 3.6. In the application to endomorphism rings, first reduce π0R to an Fp-algebra using the nilpotent ideal generated by p.
hypotheses: r≥1, i≥1; the algebra variant uses the stated restricted acyclic domain.
Universe bounds are fixed explicitly; changing universe uses the specified enlargement comparisons.
proofSteps: Apply restricted truncating nilinvariance to Z/p^r→Fp.
The finite-field calculation gives K(Fp)^∧p≃HZp; positive telescopes annihilate it.

For an Fp-algebra use the K(Fp)-module structure of its K-theory; for a Z/p^r-algebra use the same nilpotent reduction. The multiplicative interface is supplied explicitly before this consequence is used.
acceptance: Every positive-height telescope kills K(Fp); no vanishing is asserted at T0.

sources.match: Uses finite-field K and nilinvariance to eliminate p-power coefficient rings.

nodes.title: Products and coefficient actions on enhanced K-theory
nodes.statement: A biexact pairing C×D→E of small stable categories induces K(C)⊗K(D)→K(E), coherently with composition and units. In particular K of an E∞-ring is an E∞-ring, and K of an associative R-algebra is a module over K(R) when R is E∞. Compare with the parent’s classical products; the enhanced extension uses the stable S-construction and its nonconnective suspension compatibility. This target asserts no construction of localizing motives.
hypotheses: Pairings are separately exact; the coefficient ring R is E∞ for the module assertion.
Universe bounds are fixed explicitly; changing universe uses the specified enlargement comparisons.
proofSteps: Apply the multivariable S-construction to a separately exact pairing and check shuffle/interchange coherence.
Extend across nonconnective suspension using the compatible exact tensor pairings.
For modules over a commutative ring use relative tensor product; track the unit and the projection formula for transfer.
acceptance: For finite projective modules over a discrete commutative ring, the product on K0 is the existing tensor-product multiplication.

sources.locator: Theorem 5.8, Proposition 5.9 and Corollaries 5.10–5.11, manuscript p.23
sources.match: Establishes coherent lax symmetric monoidal structures on connective and nonconnective K, giving ring and module structures from separately exact tensor pairings.

sources.locator: Proof of Proposition 3.6, p.1023; Theorem B discussion, p.1014
sources.match: Uses K(Fp)-module actions and K(R)’s E∞ structure.

nodes.title: Acyclic additive and stable categories
nodes.statement: Let n≥1 and C be small idempotent-complete additive. If every hom_C(X,X) is L_n^{p,f}-acyclic, then Kadd(C) is T(i)-acyclic for 1≤i≤n. If C is stable and every full End_C(X) is L_n^{p,f}-acyclic, then K(C) is T(i)-acyclic in the same range. The stable conclusion follows by the S-construction and does not import Levy’s later chromatic corollary.
hypotheses: n≥1; C is small idempotent-complete additive or stable as stated.
Use connective hom endomorphisms in the additive case and full End spectra in the stable case.
Universe bounds are fixed explicitly; changing universe uses the specified enlargement comparisons.
proofSteps: Reduce additive C to one generator using filtered finite-generator subcategories.
Apply additive Morita; the endomorphism ring R is connective and acyclic. Its π0 has p-power characteristic because T0=S[1/p] is included.
Apply truncation, nilinvariance and finite-field module vanishing to K(R).

For stable C, finite-diagram mapping spectra are finite limits of cross Hom spectra, hence remain acyclic; delooping through S• and positive-height acyclicity of coconnective differences gives the full K statement.
acceptance: The stable part tests all full End spectra; checking only π0End or only mapping spaces is insufficient.

sources.match: Proves the additive and stable vanishing statements by Morita reduction and S-delooping.

nodes.title: Compact chromatic kernel for ring modules
nodes.statement: For any E1-ring A and n≥0, the localization Perf(A)→Perf(L_n^{p,f}A) has compact kernel thickly generated by A⊗F, where F ranges over finite p-primary spectra of type greater than n. Thus K(C>n⊗Perf(A))→K(A)→K(L_n^{p,f}A) is a fiber sequence. The finite p-primary condition retains the correct global T0=S[1/p] convention.
hypotheses: A is any E1-ring; n≥0; finite kernel generators are p-primary of type >n.
Universe bounds are fixed explicitly; changing universe uses the specified enlargement comparisons.
proofSteps: Smashing localization commutes with A-modules and its kernel is generated by these finite tensors.
Apply compact localization and identify End_A(A⊗F)≃DF⊗F⊗A.
Use duality, thick closure and chromatic acyclicity to show all full mapping spectra in the kernel have the needed finite-localization acyclicity.
acceptance: For n=0 the finite p-torsion generators yield p-inversion; replacing T0 globally by HQ changes the kernel.

sources.match: Identifies the compact kernel and its endomorphism spectra.

nodes.title: Mitchell vanishing and the p-inverted sphere
nodes.statement: For every i≥2, L_T(i)K(Z)=0 and L_T(i)K(S[1/p])=0. The first follows from Mitchell’s stronger periodic vanishing, not from identifying T(i) with K(i) on all spectra. For the second use the localization K(Fp)→K(Z)→K(Z[1/p]), then Waldhausen’s p-adic comparison K(S[1/p])→K(Z[1/p]).
hypotheses: p is any prime and i≥2.
Universe bounds are fixed explicitly; changing universe uses the specified enlargement comparisons.
proofSteps: Use Mitchell’s factorization of the unit into K(Z) through the image-of-J space and its vanishing vn-periodic homotopy above height one.
Apply the finite type-i ring-spectrum test: the image of a vn-element is nilpotent, so the corresponding telescope smash with K(Z) vanishes.
Use Quillen localization and K(Fp) positive-height vanishing, then apply the p-inverted sphere comparison.
acceptance: This is a height≥2 theorem: K(Z) need not be T1-acyclic.

sources.locator: Theorems A–B, pp.607–609; Theorem 3.8 and proof, pp.621–622
sources.match: The proof establishes vanishing of periodic telescope tests in addition to Morava K-homology.
Uses Mitchell and Waldhausen to kill the p-inverted bottom corner.

nodes.title: Theorem A in both forms
nodes.statement: For any E1-ring A and n≥1, A→L_n^{p,f}A induces an equivalence on L_T(i)K for every 1≤i≤n. For n≥2, A→L_(T(1)∨⋯∨T(n))A also induces a T(n)-equivalence on K. The latter removes the T0 part only after Mitchell vanishing; neither assertion is yet the two-adjacent-height Purity Theorem.
hypotheses: A is any E1-ring.
Part (i) has n≥1 and 1≤i≤n; part (ii) has n≥2.
Universe bounds are fixed explicitly; changing universe uses the specified enlargement comparisons.
proofSteps: Apply localization at the finite chromatic kernel and the acyclic-category theorem to prove the first part.
Use the fracture square separating T0 from T1∨⋯∨Tn and the replacement-algebra pullback theorem.
Kill the bottom p-inverted terms by their K(S[1/p])-module structures and Mitchell’s theorem.
acceptance: The comparison is natural for arbitrary nonconnective E1-rings. The second assertion is used only for n≥2.

sources.locator: Theorem A, p.1013; Theorem 3.8 and proof, pp.1024–1025
sources.match: States and proves the finite-localization and T0-removed variants.

nodes.title: High-height connective-cover invariance
nodes.statement: For every E1-ring A and n≥2, K(τ≥0A)→K(A) is a T(n)-equivalence. This follows from the T0-removed half of Theorem A and positive-height invariance of connective covers of spectra; it does not use CMNN vanishing or purity.
hypotheses: A is any E1-ring and n≥2.
Universe bounds are fixed explicitly; changing universe uses the specified enlargement comparisons.
proofSteps: The ring map τ≥0A→A is a T(i)-equivalence for every i≥1.
Apply Theorem A(ii), so both sides have equivalent T(n)-local K-theory after localization at T1∨⋯∨Tn.
acceptance: The height bound n≥2 is essential; no connective-cover invariance for T1 is asserted.

sources.match: Uses Theorem 3.8, before invoking purity.

nodes.title: The high-height cyclotomic trace
nodes.statement: For any E1-ring A and n≥2 the natural zigzag K(A)←K(τ≥0A)→TC(τ≥0A) consists of T(n)-equivalences. TC here is the integral theory with its natural trace; the conclusion is telescopic. Its proof uses Theorem A, DGM and Mitchell, and is independent of CMNN vanishing and purity.
hypotheses: A is any E1-ring and n≥2; TC is applied to τ≥0A.
Universe bounds are fixed explicitly; changing universe uses the specified enlargement comparisons.
proofSteps: Reduce to connective A by the preceding comparison.
Apply DGM to A→Hπ0A; the fiber of K→TC is unchanged by the connective truncation map because it is a π0-isomorphism.

For the discrete ring π0A, both K(π0A) and TC(π0A) are modules over K(Z), the latter through the cyclotomic trace and multiplicative TC. Mitchell annihilates both at T(n), n≥2. Thus DGM gives the required K→TC equivalence without a separate TC(Z) calculation.
acceptance: For A=S or a periodic E1-ring, the comparison still uses TC of the connective cover, rather than TC(A).

sources.locator: Corollary 4.30 and first proof paragraph, p.1035
sources.match: Derives the zigzag from Theorem 3.8, DGM and Mitchell alone.

nodes.title: The finite-group K-theory transfer comparison
nodes.statement: For a stable category C with coherent Cp-action, form the genuine Cp-spectrum of algebraic K-theory of its finite-group action categories using restriction and induction. For C=Perf(R) with trivial action, its underlying spectrum is K(R), its genuine fixed points are K(Fun(BCp,Perf(R))), and the transfer factors as K(R)hCp→K(R[Cp])→K(Fun(BCp,Perf(R))). Its geometric fixed-point cofiber maps to K(R)^tCp through the genuine-to-Borel comparison.
hypotheses: C is stable with coherent Cp-action; the displayed factorization uses trivial action on Perf(R).
Universe bounds are fixed explicitly; changing universe uses the specified enlargement comparisons.
proofSteps: Construct induction/restriction on equivariant perfect categories and verify double-coset/additivity identities, giving a spectral Mackey functor.
For Cp identify the proper-orbit term in isotropy separation with K(R)hCp.
Identify induction from the free action with the group-ring module functor and compare the genuine fixed-point cofiber to the Tate cofiber.
acceptance: For trivial Cp-action, the first assembly map has source K(R)⊗Σ∞_+BCp, and its composite with the quotient comparison is the norm.

nodes.title: CMNN finite-sphere vanishing
nodes.statement: For n≥2, L_T(n)K(L_(n−2)^{p,f}S)=0. The inductive proof is carried out using only Theorem A and the high-height trace comparison, not purity. Write m=n−2. The Tate-height converse reduces the step to T(m+1)-acyclicity of K(L_m^{p,f}S)^tCp.
hypotheses: n≥2; the coefficient sphere has finite localization index n−2.
Universe bounds are fixed explicitly; changing universe uses the specified enlargement comparisons.
proofSteps: Start the induction at the p-inverted sphere, using Mitchell vanishing.
Put R=L_m^{p,f}S. In the transfer factorization, the cofiber of K(R[Cp])→K(Fun(BCp,Perf(R))) is K of the Tate Verdier quotient, a module over K(R^tCp).
Kuhn’s finite blueshift gives R^tCp an L_(m−1)^{p,f}S-algebra structure; the induction hypothesis annihilates this cofiber at T(m+1).

For the first transfer factor use the high-height trace comparison on connective covers. Hesselholt–Nikolaus identifies the TC assembly cofiber in the localizing subcategory generated by τ≥0R, hence it is T(m+1)-acyclic. Handle the m=0 boundary by the base case.
The transfer is now a T(m+1)-equivalence. Geometric-fixed-point comparison annihilates K(R)^tCp at T(m+1), and the commutative-ring Tate-height converse yields the desired T(m+2) vanishing.
acceptance: No path from this node to purity is allowed in its prerequisite graph.

sources.locator: Theorem 1.1, p.1013; Remark 3.9 and proof, pp.1025–1026
sources.match: Reproduces the CMNN argument in the order needed to avoid circularity.

sources.locator: Theorem 4.6 and proof, manuscript pp.19–20; Theorem 4.10 with proof, §4.2, p.21
sources.match: Separately proves the Tate-height converse and the finite-localization vanishing theorem; these are different numbered results in this version.

nodes.title: The chromatic purity theorem
nodes.statement: For every E1-ring A, prime p and n≥1, the localization A→L_(T(n−1)∨T(n))A induces an equivalence L_T(n)K(A)≃L_T(n)K(L_(T(n−1)∨T(n))A). Equivalently, any map of E1-rings which is a T(n−1)∨T(n)-equivalence induces a T(n)-equivalence on K. At n=1 use T0=S[1/p], not HQ on arbitrary unlocalized spectra.
hypotheses: A is any E1-ring and n≥1; the bottom convention is T0=S[1/p].
Universe bounds are fixed explicitly; changing universe uses the specified enlargement comparisons.
proofSteps: For n=1 the adjacent pair is the first finite localization, so Theorem A suffices.
For n≥2 use the chromatic fracture square separating the top adjacent pair from L_(n−2)^{p,f}.
Apply the replacement-algebra invariant pullback comparison; all lower corners have K-theory modules over K(L_(n−2)^{p,f}S), annihilated by CMNN.
Use Theorem A to compare the finite-localized input with A and check functoriality for maps.
acceptance: If A is both T(n−1)- and T(n)-acyclic, L_T(n)K(A)=0.

sources.locator: Purity Theorem and proof, pp.1013 and 1025
sources.match: Combines Theorem A with CMNN to retain only the adjacent pair.

nodes.title: Connective nilpotent comparisons for K and TC
nodes.statement: If f:A→B is a map of connective E1-rings, π0f is surjective with nilpotent kernel, and f is a T1∨⋯∨Tn-equivalence for n≥1, then K(f) and TC(f) are T1∨⋯∨Tn-equivalences. If instead f is a T0-equivalence with the same π0 condition, both K(f) and TC(f) are T0-equivalences. Keep these variants separate from the arbitrary-ring purity statement.
hypotheses: The rings are connective and π0f is surjective with nilpotent kernel.
The positive-height hypothesis has n≥1; the T0 variant is a separate comparison.
Universe bounds are fixed explicitly; changing universe uses the specified enlargement comparisons.
proofSteps: Use purity height by height and the bottom fracture square to isolate the p-inverted comparison.
Apply Waldhausen truncation there and nilpotent invariance after the relevant rational/p-adic passage.
Apply the DGM cartesian square to transfer the K equivalence to TC; prove the rational/T0 variant by the corresponding truncation argument.
acceptance: A π0-isomorphism is allowed; a general ring map with no nilpotent π0 condition is not covered by this connective variant.

sources.match: States the positive-height and bottom-height versions with their nilpotence hypothesis.

nodes.title: Theorem B and vanishing for algebras
nodes.statement: For an E∞-ring R, ht(K(R))≤ht(R)+1 in the chromatic height convention ht(R)=inf{h≥−1:T(h+1)⊗R=0}, with infinity allowed. More precisely, if R is T(n)-acyclic for n≥0 and B is any E1 R-algebra, then K(B) is T(n+i)-acyclic for every i≥1. At n=0 the acyclicity hypothesis is R[1/p]=0.
hypotheses: R is E∞; B is an E1 R-algebra in the refined version; n≥0.
Universe bounds are fixed explicitly; changing universe uses the specified enlargement comparisons.
proofSteps: Use Hahn to propagate T(n)-acyclicity of the commutative coefficient ring to every higher height.
Every B-module spectrum is R-linear, so B is acyclic at each such height.
Apply purity to each pair of adjacent heights of B to annihilate its K-theory; translate the vanishing into the extended-integer height inequality.
acceptance: For an E∞-ring of height n≥0, the conclusion is ht(KR)≤n+1; it does not yet assert nonvanishing at n+1.

sources.match: Derives the height bound and the stronger algebra-valued vanishing statement.

nodes.title: Yuan’s Lubin–Tate nonvanishing input
nodes.statement: For Lubin–Tate E_n associated to a height-n formal group over a perfect characteristic-p field, n≥1, L_T(n+1)K(E_n)≠0. This is an imported converse input with its proof dependencies recorded: purity is already proved before it is used. The intermediary result says that T(j)⊗E≠0 for E∞ E implies T(j)⊗K(E^tCp)≠0, j≥1.
hypotheses: n≥1; E_n comes from a finite-height formal group over a perfect characteristic-p field.
Universe bounds are fixed explicitly; changing universe uses the specified enlargement comparisons.
proofSteps: Use the residual circle action on E^tCp and the circle-equivariant THH universal property to map its K-theory into (e^tCp)^h(S1/Cp), where e is the connective cover.
Invoke the Tate-orbit comparison and the circle-Tate calculation to preserve T(j)-nonzero targets; use purity to replace E by e at the Cp-Tate step.
For E_(n+1)^tCp use telescopic K étale descent to choose a strict henselization with nonzero T(n+1)-local K.
Use the Lubin–Tate mapping property over its K(n)-local strict henselian height-n localization to obtain an E_n-algebra with nonzero K; nonvanishing pulls back along the unital K map.
acceptance: The source’s Theorem 3.1 is the two-height purity statement despite its attribution to “Theorem A”; the actual dependency here is purity.

sources.locator: Theorems A and C, manuscript pp.2–3; §3 proof pp.6–7; §4, Theorem 4.2 and Lemma 4.5, pp.7–9
sources.match: Proves the nonvanishing through Tate actions, strict henselizations and the Lubin–Tate universal property.

nodes.title: The height-zero lower bound
nodes.statement: For an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field L, let E0(L)=HL[u±1] with |u|=2. Then K(E0(L))^∧p≃ku^∧p⊕Σku^∧p, and in particular L_T1K(E0(L))≠0. This is the height-zero periodic field input needed to include n=0 in redshift; it is not Yuan’s positive-height theorem.
hypotheses: L is algebraically closed of characteristic zero; u has degree 2.
Universe bounds are fixed explicitly; changing universe uses the specified enlargement comparisons.
proofSteps: Use Suslin rigidity/comparison to identify K(L)^∧p with ku^∧p.
Apply regular localization to HL[u]→HL[u±1]. The first K(L)→K(HL[u]) map is induced by restriction through the u-torsion quotient.
By additivity its composite with the connective truncation comparison is id plus an odd suspension, hence zero; split the resulting cofiber sequence after p-completion.
acceptance: E0(L) has height zero and K(E0(L)) has nonzero height-one part.

sources.match: Gives the split calculation using Suslin and regular devissage.

nodes.title: Redshift at nonnegative height
nodes.statement: For every p-local E∞-ring R with ht(R)≥0, ht(K(R))=ht(R)+1, allowing infinity+1=infinity. More generally this holds for any E∞ R of positive height, and for a global height-zero R provided R⊗HQ≠0. At finite positive height n, the Nullstellensatz gives a map from the nonzero T(n)-localization to E_n(L), L algebraically closed of characteristic p; at height zero it is applied to the nonzero rationalization and L has characteristic zero. The global bottom convention T0=S[1/p] alone does not imply that rationalization is nonzero; source issue E1 records this restriction. No equality is asserted at ht(R)=−1.
hypotheses: R is E∞ with ht(R)≥0.
At height zero additionally R⊗HQ≠0; this follows automatically if R is p-local.
Universes and the global T0 convention are fixed.
proofSteps: At finite positive height use the Nullstellensatz on the nonzero T(n)-local E∞-ring. At height zero apply its n=0 case only to R⊗HQ, assumed nonzero, to obtain the characteristic-zero field map.
Purity and the lower-bound input give T(n+1)-nonvanishing of K(R); combine with the upper bound.
If ht(R)=infinity, apply the same detection to each finite height and use the lower-bound maps to obtain arbitrarily high nonvanishing.
Record the negative-height counterexample separately: at p=2, F2^tC2 is 1-periodic, so its K-theory vanishes after inverting 2 by additivity and has height −1 rather than 0.
acceptance: For every n≥0 the periodic field E_n has K-theory of height n+1. The excluded negative-height example prevents an incorrect universal equality.

sources.locator: Corollary 5.2 (Theorem D), pp.3 and 55; Theorem 9.11 and Remark 9.13, manuscript pp.88–90
sources.match: Uses chromatic field detection to combine the upper and lower redshift bounds.

sources.locator: Redshift Theorem and following discussion, p.1014
sources.match: States the nonnegative-height restriction and attributes the converse.

nodes.title: Both heights in purity are necessary
nodes.statement: For each n≥1 the functor A↦L_T(n)K(A) on E1-rings does not factor through A↦L_T(n)A and does not factor through A↦L_T(n−1)A. These are assertions that each putative universal factorization fails, rather than that every individual map to a single-height localization fails.
hypotheses: n≥1; factorization means one valid for every E1-ring.
Universe bounds are fixed explicitly; changing universe uses the specified enlargement comparisons.
proofSteps: To rule out factorization through T(n), choose a height-(n−1) commutative ring with nonzero T(n)-local K: use E_(n−1) for n≥2 and the height-zero input for n=1.
For factorization through T(n−1), choose a connective spectrum M that is T(n−1)-acyclic but T(n)-nonzero, and use split square-zero extensions S⊕Σ^rM→S.

If all these K comparisons were T(n)-equivalences, their stabilized relative K colimit would vanish. Stable K with coefficients in M is a fixed suspension of M by the imported derivative theorem, a contradiction. Verify the coefficient/shift convention at the import boundary; any fixed shift gives the contradiction.
acceptance: The n=1 case uses a height-zero ring rather than an undefined E_(−1); the square-zero argument requires an actual separated telescope input.

sources.match: Gives the height-(n−1) and square-zero counterexamples to the two universal factorizations.

nodes.title: Nice maps of connective E∞-rings
nodes.statement: A map f:R→S of connective E∞-rings is n-nice, n≥0, if π0R→π0S is an isomorphism identified with the identity of Z and f is an HQ∨T1∨⋯∨Tn-equivalence. It is nice if it is n-nice for every n≥0. The rational summand is HQ here by definition; it is not a global replacement of T0. Record both the chosen identifications with Z and the compatibility of π0f.
hypotheses: R,S are connective E∞ with compatible fixed π0 identifications with Z; n≥0.
Universe bounds are fixed explicitly; changing universe uses the specified enlargement comparisons.
proofSteps: Define the predicate with actual connective E∞ input rings and fixed π0 identifications.
Separate its rational comparison from the finite list of positive telescopes.
Check preservation under identity/composition and under equivalence of the chosen π0 models.
acceptance: K preserves n-nice maps and nice maps by the following theorem, not by definition.

nodes.title: K preserves nice maps
nodes.statement: If f:R→S is n-nice, then K(f):K(R)→K(S) is n-nice; therefore K preserves nice maps. Here K(R) and K(S) are connective E∞-rings with π0=Z: nonpositive comparison and K_i(Z)=0 for i<0, K0(Z)=Z establish those claims before iterating.
hypotheses: f is n-nice, with the output ring structure on K supplied by multiplicativity.
Universe bounds are fixed explicitly; changing universe uses the specified enlargement comparisons.
proofSteps: Use nonpositive comparison to prove the output connectivity and π0 identifications.
Apply the positive-height connective nilpotent comparison, where π0f is an isomorphism.
Use rational Waldhausen truncation for the rational piece; assemble the n-nice predicate.
acceptance: The output is a map of rings, not merely a map of spectra; its π0 identifications are required for a second application of K.

sources.match: Proves preservation of n-nice maps, including connectivity and π0.

nodes.title: Iterated finite p-power K-theory
nodes.statement: For r≥1 the rank map K(Z/p^r)→HZ is nice. Consequently for j≥1 the natural iterated map K^j(Z/p^r)→K^(j−1)(Z) is an HQ∨T1∨⋯∨Tn-equivalence for every n≥0. The initial map is induced by rank on the connective E∞ K-spectrum; it is not a ring map Z/p^r→Z.
hypotheses: r≥1, j≥1 and n≥0.
Universe bounds are fixed explicitly; changing universe uses the specified enlargement comparisons.
proofSteps: Use negative-K nilinvariance and the finite-field computation to identify π≤0K(Z/p^r).
Use positive telescope vanishing and the rational nilinvariance/p-power relative-K input to show the rank map is nice.
Iterate preservation of nice maps, maintaining all connective ring structures and π0=Z.
acceptance: At r=1, K(Fp)→HZ is rationally equivalent and is an equivalence at every positive telescope, although it is not an integral equivalence.

sources.match: Derives the rank comparison and its iteration.
Supplies rational nilpotent invariance when p is nilpotent.

nodes.title: K-theory of Morava K-theory
nodes.statement: Let m≥1 and K(m) be the standard E1 Morava K-theory at p, with connective cover k(m) and π*k(m)=Fp[v_m], |v_m|=2p^m−2. Then L_T(i)K(K(m))=0 for i∉{0,m,m+1}. Separately, after inverting p, K(K(m))[1/p]≃K(Fp)[1/p]⊕ΣK(Fp)[1/p]. The vanishing statement does not assert that each of the three exceptional heights is nonzero.
hypotheses: m≥1; use the standard E1 coefficient Morava K-theory and connective k(m).
Universe bounds are fixed explicitly; changing universe uses the specified enlargement comparisons.
proofSteps: Use the known chromatic support of the E1 Morava coefficient ring and purity at all disjoint adjacent pairs.
Apply regular devissage to k(m)→K(m); the fiber is K(Fp).

Compare K(k(m))[1/p] with K(Fp)[1/p] by the p-power truncation argument. The devissage map composes with this comparison as id plus the odd shift 2p^m−1, hence is zero by additivity; split its cofiber.
acceptance: At m=1 only heights 0,1,2 can remain; the [1/p] splitting is a different assertion from T0-local comparison.

sources.match: Gives the support bound and the rational-away-from-p split calculation.

nodes.title: K-theory of truncated spheres
nodes.statement: For every r≥0 and i≥2, L_T(i)K(τ≤rS)=0. The input is a connective finite Postnikov truncation of the sphere; this gives no such vanishing claim for K(S) itself.
hypotheses: r≥0 and i≥2.
Universe bounds are fixed explicitly; changing universe uses the specified enlargement comparisons.
proofSteps: The finite Postnikov ring is acyclic at every positive telescope.
For i≥2 both T(i−1) and T(i) annihilate it, so purity applies.
acceptance: At r=0 this recovers the high-height vanishing of K(Z).

sources.match: Applies purity to sphere Postnikov truncations.

nodes.title: Truncated Brown–Peterson localization
nodes.statement: For n≥0, K(BP⟨n⟩)→K(E(n)) is a T(i)-equivalence for i≥n+1 and these spectra are T(i)-acyclic for i≥n+2. For n≥1 the usual sequence K(BP⟨n−1⟩)→K(BP⟨n⟩)→K(E(n)) is a fiber sequence after L_(⊕i≥n+1 T(i)); the first arrow is the restriction/devissage map through the quotient. It is not asserted to be an unlocalized fiber sequence.
hypotheses: n≥0; the displayed three-term sequence has n≥1 and is localized.
Universe bounds are fixed explicitly; changing universe uses the specified enlargement comparisons.
proofSteps: Use the chromatic localization behavior of BP⟨n⟩→E(n) and apply the adjacent-pair test.
Use support above height n to deduce the higher vanishing.

For the localized sequence the low-height term vanishes as required and localization identifies the last two terms; retain the restriction map and do not assert an integral localization theorem without regularity.
acceptance: For n≥2 the corresponding rational/unlocalized fiber sequence can fail; the localized statement must survive that negative control.

sources.match: States the localized equivalences and warns against the unlocalized sequence.

nodes.title: Purity for suspension A-theory
nodes.statement: Let W be pointed connected and n≥1. If the reduced suspension spectrum Σ∞W is T(n−1)∨T(n)-acyclic, then A(*)→A(ΣW)→A(*) are T(n)-equivalences. The suspension is reduced and the coefficient ring is Σ∞_+ΩΣW.
hypotheses: W is pointed connected and reduced Σ∞W is T(n−1)∨T(n)-acyclic; n≥1.
Universe bounds are fixed explicitly; changing universe uses the specified enlargement comparisons.
proofSteps: Use the James splitting of Σ∞_+ΩΣW as the tensor algebra on the reduced Σ∞W.
Its augmentation to S has fiber built from positive tensor powers of Σ∞W, still acyclic at the adjacent pair.
Apply purity to the augmentation and use its unit splitting.
acceptance: W contractible gives the identity equivalence A(*)≃A(ΣW).

sources.match: Combines the James splitting with purity.

nodes.title: K-theory of James-filtered Thom spectra
nodes.statement: For m≥1, the map y(m)→Fp induces an L_(m−1)^{p,f}-equivalence on K, so K(y(m)) is T(i)-acyclic for 0<i<m. At p=2 the integral analogue z(m)→HZ_(2) induces a T(i)-equivalence on K for 0<i<m. The z(m) statement does not include the bottom T0 summand.
hypotheses: m≥1; z(m) is the prime-two integral analogue and its range is 0<i<m.
Universe bounds are fixed explicitly; changing universe uses the specified enlargement comparisons.
proofSteps: Import the precise connectivity, π0 and chromatic acyclicity properties of the Thom spectra.
Apply the connective nilpotent comparison and its rational part to y(m).
Apply only the positive-height comparison to z(m), and use finite-field K vanishing for the y(m) conclusion.
acceptance: For m=1 the displayed positive-height range is empty; the finite-localization assertion for y(1) still has its bottom-height meaning.

sources.match: States the y(m) and prime-two z(m) consequences with different ranges.

nodes.title: Telescopic K-theory Galois descent
nodes.statement: Let A→B be a finite-group G-Galois extension of E∞-rings. Suppose B is perfect over A and the transfer K0(B)⊗Q→K0(A)⊗Q has 1 in its image. For every prime and finite chromatic localization L_n^f, n≥0, both canonical maps L_n^fK(A)→L_n^f(K(B)^hG)→(L_n^fK(B))^hG are equivalences. Consequently the analogous maps after any positive T(i)-localization are equivalences. The commutation with homotopy fixed points is a conclusion under these hypotheses, not a formal property of localization.
hypotheses: A→B is finite G-Galois E∞, B is perfect over A, and rational K0 transfer hits 1.
Universe bounds are fixed explicitly; changing universe uses the specified enlargement comparisons.
proofSteps: Use the transfer projection formula to obtain the rational unit-generation condition in the additive motive category of A-linear perfect categories.
Apply CMNN’s ε-nilpotent descent argument to the Amitsur augmented cosimplicial object; record the needed weakly additive motive interface as an RT.5 supplier request.
Its totalization tower becomes rapidly convergent after finite periodic localization, so localization can be moved through this particular totalization.

Identify the Galois Amitsur diagram with the G-cobar diagram. Apply the same ε-nilpotent tower argument directly for each T(i), using CMNN Remark 2.9 and Proposition 2.19, to justify both T(i)-localized comparison maps; this is not inferred by commuting a further localization with arbitrary homotopy fixed points.
acceptance: For G=1 all maps are identities. For nontrivial G, a Galois label alone does not discharge the rational-transfer hypothesis.

sources.locator: Theorem 5.6 and proof, manuscript p.22; Theorem 5.1 pp.20–21; Proposition 2.19 pp.12–13; Remark 2.9, p.9
sources.match: Derives Galois descent and the two localization/totalization maps from rational transfer.

nodes.title: Rational transfer for higher real K-theories
nodes.statement: Let E be Lubin–Tate theory of a finite-height formal group over a perfect characteristic-p field k, and H a finite subgroup of the automorphism group of the pair (formal group,k), allowing semilinear field automorphisms. Then K0(E)⊗Q→K0(E^hH)⊗Q is surjective. In particular the transfer condition for telescopic K-descent holds for E^hH→E.
hypotheses: H is finite in the semilinear automorphism group of the formal-group/field pair.
Universe bounds are fixed explicitly; changing universe uses the specified enlargement comparisons.
proofSteps: Use CMNN Appendix B’s finite even H-complex X with nonzero finite-free twisted Morava K-cohomology; this representation-theoretic chromatic construction is requested from CH.7.
Lift the free basis to obtain E⊗DX≃coind_H(E)^r as semilinear modules and descend to E^hH⊗DX≃E^r.
The transferred class is M times the unit, where M>0 is the number of even cells of X. The transfer image is an ideal by the projection formula, so rationalizing makes it the whole K0.
acceptance: The argument retains the field-automorphism factor; at p=3 it applies to the full order-24 supersingular group.

sources.locator: Theorem B.2 and Corollaries B.3–B.4, manuscript pp.37–39
sources.match: Constructs an even free-detecting complex and proves rational-transfer surjectivity.

nodes.title: Purity for ko-algebras
nodes.statement: For any E1 ko-algebra A at the chosen prime, inverting the central Bott class β induces a T(i)-equivalence K(A)→K(A[β−1]) for every i≥2. For i≥3, L_T(i)K(A)=0. No regularity or connectivity assumption on the ko-algebra A is required.
hypotheses: A is an E1 ko-algebra; the class β is central Bott.
Universe bounds are fixed explicitly; changing universe uses the specified enlargement comparisons.
proofSteps: The ko→KO Bott localization is an equivalence on the adjacent heights relevant for i≥2.
Base change to A preserves this equivalence; apply purity.
Use the commutative ko coefficient ring’s height-one bound and the algebra-valued vanishing theorem.
acceptance: For A=ko this compares K(ko) with K(KO) at every T(i), i≥2.

sources.match: Proves Bott-localization purity and the height-three-and-above vanishing.

nodes.title: Purity for tmf-algebras
nodes.statement: For any E1 tmf-algebra A, K(A) is T(i)-acyclic for i≥4. The map K(A)→K(A⊗tmf Tmf) is a T(i)-equivalence for i≥2, and K(A)→K(A⊗tmf TMF) is a T(3)-equivalence. Here Tmf is the nonconnective compactified global-sections spectrum and TMF the periodic open-moduli spectrum; the two are not identified.
hypotheses: A is an E1 tmf-algebra; the indicated height ranges differ for Tmf and TMF.
Universe bounds are fixed explicitly; changing universe uses the specified enlargement comparisons.
proofSteps: Import the distinct chromatic comparisons tmf→Tmf and tmf→TMF from the modular homotopy owner.
Base change those E∞ coefficient maps to A and apply purity at each stated adjacent pair.
Apply the algebra-valued upper bound from the height-two coefficient ring.
acceptance: With A=tmf the T(2) comparison is with Tmf; the displayed periodic TMF comparison is asserted at T(3).

sources.match: Gives the algebra-valued modular applications.

nodes.title: Supersingular fixed-point description
nodes.statement: At p=2, L_T3K(tmf)≃L_T3(K(E2)^hGL2(F3))≃(L_T3K(E2))^hGL2(F3). At p=3 replace GL2(F3) by the full order-24 supersingular stabilizer G24, including the residue-field Galois action. The intermediate T(3)-localized K(TMF) is equivalent to the same spectra. The raw K(tmf)≃K(E2)^hG equivalence is not claimed.
hypotheses: p=2 or 3, with the full group specified for each prime.
Universe bounds are fixed explicitly; changing universe uses the specified enlargement comparisons.
proofSteps: Use the modular chromatic comparison to replace tmf by periodic TMF at T3.
Identify its relevant completed height-two coefficient ring with E2^hG, retaining the full semilinear stabilizer.
Apply the rational-transfer descent theorem, now justified by Lubin–Tate transfer; use its separate fixed-point commutation assertion for the final equivalence.
acceptance: At p=2 the group has order 48; at p=3 the full group has order 24 rather than the order-12 geometric automorphism group.

sources.match: Combines modular comparison and CMNN Galois descent; the prime-three analogue is specified after the proof.

nodes.title: Classical regular localization checks
nodes.statement: Recover the known connective localization sequences Kconn(Z)→Kconn(ko)→Kconn(KO) and Kconn(Z)→Kconn(tmf)→Kconn(Tmf) with the coefficient localization and any necessary prime localization matched to the chosen model. Their fiber identifications require the regular/coherent module devissage hypotheses, unlike the general algebra-valued purity comparisons. Record the K(Z)-fiber as the source of high-height equivalence, not as a proof of those sequences for all coefficient algebras.
hypotheses: Use the regularity/coherent-support hypotheses for ko and tmf; coefficient prime localization follows the chosen models.
Universe bounds are fixed explicitly; changing universe uses the specified enlargement comparisons.
proofSteps: For ko invoke the regular devissage model and identify the Bott-torsion category with the indicated Z-linear heart.
For tmf use the regularity and support description of coherent modules on the compactified moduli stack; request the exact supplier statement in CH.12.
Compare these classical fibers with the purity conclusions after telescopic localization.
acceptance: The general tmf-algebra case is supplied by purity and does not inherit a K(Z) fiber without regularity.

sources.match: Explains regular-localization instances and distinguishes them from the algebra-valued conclusions.

nodes.title: Height-one truncation and p-inversion
nodes.statement: If A is a K(1)-acyclic E1-ring, then K(A)→K(A[1/p]) is a K(1)-equivalence, without a connectivity restriction. If A is additionally connective, K(A)→K(π0A) is a K(1)-equivalence. The equality of T(1)- and K(1)-localization is the known height-one comparison, not the telescope conjecture at arbitrary height.
hypotheses: A is K1-acyclic E1.
Only the comparison with π0A requires A connective.
Universe bounds are fixed explicitly; changing universe uses the specified enlargement comparisons.
proofSteps: Apply purity to A→A[1/p], since the T0 comparison is automatic and both T1 terms vanish.
For connective A use Waldhausen’s p-adic truncation on A[1/p].
Compare with the discrete π0 ring, keeping the connective assumption exactly at the truncation step.
acceptance: Every discrete ring is K(1)-acyclic, so its K(1)-local K-theory is unchanged by inverting p.

sources.match: Separates arbitrary-ring p-inversion from connective truncation.

nodes.title: Nilinvariance, Milnor excision and cdh-descent
nodes.statement: On discrete rings, L_K1K is nilinvariant and carries Milnor squares with a surjective side to pullback squares. For a qcqs scheme X, the invariant X↦L_K1K(Perf(X)) satisfies cdh-descent, using Nisnevich descent and abstract blowup squares with proper finitely presented modification and finitely presented closed immersion, as in LT Appendix A. Arbitrary closed immersions require the filtered-continuity extension in Remark A.3. The scheme statement is the extension through perfect complexes, not a topology on arbitrary noncommutative rings.
hypotheses: Ring inputs are discrete; scheme inputs are qcqs and evaluated on Perf.
Universe bounds are fixed explicitly; changing universe uses the specified enlargement comparisons.
proofSteps: Discrete rings are K1-acyclic, so height-one truncation gives a globally truncating invariant on ring inputs.
Apply truncating excision and nilinvariance.
Use the perfect-complex extension and Nisnevich descent, then Land–Tamme’s truncating-invariant blowup argument with the noetherian approximation/pro-descent input supplied by scheme K-theory.
acceptance: A nilpotent thickening has the same K1-local K-theory; a Milnor square without a surjective side requires additional hypotheses.

sources.match: Deduces the three descent consequences.

sources.locator: Theorem 3.3, p.29; Theorem A.2 and proof, manuscript pp.35–37
sources.match: Extends a truncating invariant to cdh descent on schemes.

nodes.title: Flat and smooth spectral affine lines
nodes.statement: For an E1-ring A define the flat polynomial algebra A[x]=A⊗Σ∞_+N. For connective A and a central E∞ sphere algebra, define A{x}=A⊗Sym_S(S), with Sym_S(S) the free E∞ sphere algebra on one degree-zero generator. The canonical A{x}→A[x] is a π0-isomorphism for connective A, but the two algebras need not be equivalent. Both retain an augmentation at x=0.
hypotheses: A is E1; the π0 comparison requires A connective.
Universe bounds are fixed explicitly; changing universe uses the specified enlargement comparisons.
proofSteps: Construct the monoid algebra and the free commutative sphere algebra, keeping their different symmetric-power constructions.
Define the comparison by the generator and compute π0 for connective A.
Compare augmentations and extension of scalars; identify the flat construction on HA with H(A[x]) for an ordinary ring A.
acceptance: The distinction is visible on the sphere: the degree-d piece of the smooth free algebra contains Σ∞_+BΣd.

sources.locator: Definition in Corollary 4.25 and Remark 4.26, pp.1033–1034
sources.match: Distinguishes the flat and free-E∞ affine lines.

api.statement: The chosen degree-zero generator induces Sym_S(S)→Σ∞_+N and hence A{x}→A[x].

api.name: TauCeti.KTheory.AffineLines.pi_zero
api.statement: For connective A, both π0 affine lines identify with π0(A)[x] and their comparison is the identity.

api.name: TauCeti.KTheory.AffineLines.augmentation
api.statement: The inclusion A→A[x] followed by x=0 is id, and likewise for A{x}.

tests.statement: For an ordinary ring R, HR[x]≃H(R[x]).

tests.name: TauCeti.KTheory.AffineLines.test_zero

The π0 comparison extends homotopy invariance to the smooth line.

nodes.title: Height-one homotopy invariance
nodes.statement: For connective K(1)-acyclic E1-ring A, the maps K(A)→K(A[x]), K(A)→K(A{x}), and K(A{x})→K(A[x]) are K(1)-equivalences. The result includes all discrete rings, with no regularity assumption. Flatness or the π0-isomorphism alone does not assert integral K-equivalence.
hypotheses: A is connective K1-acyclic E1.
Universe bounds are fixed explicitly; changing universe uses the specified enlargement comparisons.
proofSteps: The two affine lines are connective and K1-acyclic as A-modules.
First use height-one truncation to replace the flat input by its ordinary π0 polynomial ring, then use p-inversion to reduce to a Z[1/p]-algebra.
Weibel’s NK result makes multiplication by p invertible on every homotopy group of fib(K(A[x])→K(A)), so its p-completion, hence K1-localization, vanishes.
Apply height-one truncation to the smooth-to-flat π0-isomorphism and use composition to obtain the other comparisons.
acceptance: For a singular ring such as Fp[ε]/ε², this holds after K1-localization although integral polynomial invariance fails.

sources.locator: Corollary 4.25 with proof and Remark 4.26, pp.1033–1034
sources.match: Gives the complete reduction to Weibel NK and the free-E∞ extension.

nodes.title: Comparison with homotopy K-theory
nodes.statement: For every discrete ring A, K(A)→KH(A) induces L_K1K(A)≃L_K1KH(A). Import KH(A)=|K(A[Δ•])| and its simplicial structure from SchemeKTheoryOperations:S.5, with A[Δr]=A[x0,…,xr]/(Σxi−1).
hypotheses: A is a discrete ring; KH is the supplier’s simplicial polynomial model.
Universe bounds are fixed explicitly; changing universe uses the specified enlargement comparisons.
proofSteps: Each simplex algebra is a polynomial algebra in r variables, so its K1-local K agrees with that of A by repeated homotopy invariance.
Use the coherent augmented simplicial map, then the fact that localization is a left adjoint and preserves this realization.
Compare with the supplier’s specified KH model and its normalization maps.
acceptance: For regular noetherian A this agrees with the imported integral K≃KH comparison; singular A is allowed only in the localized assertion here.

sources.match: Obtains the KH comparison from polynomial homotopy invariance.

nodes.title: The height-one TC obstruction
nodes.statement: The p-completion of TC(Z[1/p]) is zero, whereas L_K1TC(Z) is nonzero. Thus the map TC(Z)→TC(Z[1/p]) is not a K(1)-equivalence, and the arbitrary-ring high-height comparison K(A)←K(τ≥0A)→TC(τ≥0A) cannot be extended to height one. The nonzero height-one TC(Z) calculation is imported from RT.3 with its prime-two variant kept separate.
hypotheses: p is fixed; the odd-prime decomposition and the prime-two calculation are separate supplier inputs.
Universe bounds are fixed explicitly; changing universe uses the specified enlargement comparisons.
proofSteps: Use the p-inverted discrete input to compute TC(Z[1/p])^∧p=0.
At odd p the known K1-local TC(Z) decomposition includes L_K1S and a suspended p-complete KU summand; at p=2 use its separately computed filtered analogue.
Compare with height-one p-inversion invariance for K and deduce failure of a height-one version of the high trace comparison.
acceptance: A nonzero direct summand at odd p, and the separately proved nonzero prime-two calculation, detect the obstruction.

sources.match: Exhibits the precise height-one failure.

nodes.title: TC does not preserve filtered category colimits
nodes.statement: Although L_K1TC commutes with filtered colimits of discrete rings, it does not commute with filtered colimits of small stable categories. The filtered colimit of Mod_(Z/p^r)(Perf(Z)) identifies with the p-power-torsion perfect Z-modules and sits in an exact sequence with Perf(Z) and Perf(Z[1/p]). Each stage has zero L_K1TC, while the colimit has nonzero L_K1TC.
hypotheses: The diagram is a filtered system of enhanced perfect categories, not a filtered system of rings.
Universe bounds are fixed explicitly; changing universe uses the specified enlargement comparisons.
proofSteps: Construct the filtered system of module categories with their compatible forgetful functors; every compact p-power-torsion perfect Z-complex belongs to a stage.
Each stage’s TC is a module over TC(Z/p^r), whose K1-localization vanishes by the finite p-power K comparison.
Use localizing TC on the p-inversion exact sequence: its fiber identifies with TC(Z) at K1 because TC(Z[1/p]) vanishes.
This gives nonzero TC of the colimit and contradicts preservation of this category colimit, without contradicting the separate ring-colimit theorem.
acceptance: The counterexample’s objects are enhanced perfect categories; replacing its colimit by a colimit of the coefficient rings changes the assertion.

sources.match: Gives this filtered category counterexample while retaining the ring-colimit theorem.

nodes.title: Chromatic consequences of the bounded-heart fiber
nodes.statement: For small stable idempotent-complete C, Kadd(C)→K(C) is a T(i)-equivalence for i≥2. If End_C(X)[1/p]=0 for every X, it is also a T1-equivalence. More generally, for a full additive subcategory A⊂C which thickly generates C, Kadd(A)→K(C) is a T(i)-equivalence for every i≥2. A need not itself be closed under every retract; the positive comparison is enough.
hypotheses: C is small stable idempotent-complete; A is full additive and thickly generates C.
The height-one conclusion requires End_C(X)[1/p]=0 for every X.
Universe bounds are fixed explicitly; changing universe uses the specified enlargement comparisons.
proofSteps: For A=C use the bounded-heart fiber; connective K(D♥) is K(Z)-linear and Mitchell kills its heights≥2. Coconnective discrepancies are also acyclic there.
Under p-inverted endomorphism vanishing, devissage of the torsion heart reduces its connective K to K(Fp) at height one.

For a general additive generator subcategory pass to finite sets of generators and their direct sum X. Compare the positive Kadd-space with K(τ≥0End_C(X)) and use stable Morita plus high-height connective-cover invariance.
acceptance: No integral equivalence Kadd(C)≃K(C) is asserted, since cofiber relations are absent from additive group completion.

sources.locator: Proposition 3.12, p.1027; Corollary 4.31 and proof, p.1035
sources.match: Gives the two proofs and the general additive-generator variant.

nodes.title: Sifted colimits of high-height K-theory
nodes.statement: For n≥2, A↦L_T(n)K(A) from all E1-rings to T(n)-local spectra preserves sifted colimits. The same is true on the full subcategory of T(n−1)-local E1-rings, whose colimits are formed by localizing ambient ring colimits. No analogous statement for arbitrary filtered colimits of stable categories under L_K1TC is inferred.
hypotheses: n≥2; the diagram is sifted in E1-rings or in the specified localized full subcategory.
Universe bounds are fixed explicitly; changing universe uses the specified enlargement comparisons.
proofSteps: Import TC/p preservation of sifted colimits on connective E1-rings.
For a sifted diagram Ai compare colim τ≥0Ai→τ≥0(colim Ai); its positive telescope localizations agree, so Theorem A compares their K-theories.
Use the high trace equivalence and mod-p detection of telescopic equivalences to move K through the colimit.
On the T(n−1)-local ring subcategory, its ambient colimit→localized colimit is an adjacent-height equivalence because T(n−1)-local spectra are T(n)-acyclic; apply purity.
acceptance: Both a filtered diagram and a geometric realization are covered. The subcategory’s colimit is not silently identified with the ambient colimit.

sources.match: Proves both sifted-colimit assertions and specifies the localized-subcategory argument.

nodes.title: Cyclic orbit diagrams and assembly
nodes.statement: For a discrete group G, let Or_Cyc(G) be the full subcategory of the G-orbit category on G/H for all cyclic H≤G, including infinite cyclic H. For an E1-ring R put R[H]=R⊗Σ∞_+H. Use the action-groupoid construction and induction of perfect modules to give a coherent functor G/H↦K(R[H]) and the analogous TC diagram. The collapse G/H→G/G gives assembly colim_OrCyc K(R[H])→K(R[G]).
hypotheses: G is any discrete group; the family contains every cyclic subgroup, finite or infinite.
Universe bounds are fixed explicitly; changing universe uses the specified enlargement comparisons.
proofSteps: Construct the transport groupoid of a G-set, then its R-linear perfect-module category; this avoids noncanonical choices of conjugating elements in orbit morphisms.
Apply the invariant and identify transitive orbits with the group-ring value.
Use the terminal orbit in Or(G) to define the natural cocone and its assembly map.
acceptance: For cyclic G, G/G belongs to Or_Cyc(G) and is terminal, so assembly is an equivalence before localization.

sources.match: Specifies the orbit family and group-ring assembly maps.

The natural high-height trace comparison transfers TC assembly to K.

nodes.title: p-adic TC assembly for cyclic subgroups
nodes.statement: For a connective E1-ring R and any discrete group G, colim_(G/H∈Or_Cyc(G))TC(R[H])→TC(R[G]) is a p-adic equivalence. The colimit is formed before p-completion. This does not assert that uncompleted p-typical TC assembly is always an equivalence.
hypotheses: R is connective E1; G is any discrete group; completion is after the orbit colimit.
Universe bounds are fixed explicitly; changing universe uses the specified enlargement comparisons.
proofSteps: Import the all-cyclic THH assembly equivalence for arbitrary G, with its compatible cyclotomic structure.
Import TC/p preservation of all small colimits of connective cyclotomic spectra; all group-ring THH inputs satisfy connectivity.
Apply TC/p to the THH assembly equivalence and use mod-p detection of p-complete equivalences.
acceptance: If G is cyclic the assertion is the terminal-orbit identity; arbitrary noncyclic and infinite groups are allowed.

sources.match: Combines THH assembly and TC/p colimit preservation, with completion on the final assembly map.

nodes.title: Telescopic Farrell–Jones assembly
nodes.statement: For every E1-ring R, every discrete group G and every n≥2, the assembly map colim_(G/H∈Or_Cyc(G))K(R[H])→K(R[G]) is a T(n)-equivalence. There is no connectivity requirement on R and the family includes infinite cyclic subgroups.
hypotheses: R is any E1-ring, G any discrete group and n≥2.
Universe bounds are fixed explicitly; changing universe uses the specified enlargement comparisons.
proofSteps: Use the natural high-height comparison on every group ring to replace K(R[H]) by TC(τ≥0R[H]).
Identify τ≥0(R[H])≃(τ≥0R)[H], since the group ring is a direct sum of copies of R as a spectrum.
Apply connective p-adic TC assembly, then positive telescopic localization; naturality identifies its map with the K assembly map.
acceptance: The proof covers periodic coefficient rings and infinite G; it does not claim the integral Farrell–Jones conjecture.

sources.match: Transfers the p-adic TC theorem through the high-height trace equivalence.

nodes.title: Continuous Witt operations on NK
nodes.statement: Let R be commutative and A a unital R-algebra. The groups NK_j(A)=ker(K_j(A[x])→K_j(A)), j∈Z, carry a natural continuous module action of the existing big Witt ring W_N>0(R), imported from HabiroRings HR.4. Each individual element is killed by the kernel of a sufficiently long initial-segment Witt truncation. Construct the action through the reduced endomorphism ring End0(R) and nilpotent endomorphism categories; negative degrees use the parent’s Bass contraction, not an invented connective-only NK.
hypotheses: R is commutative and A is a unital R-algebra; j is any integer.
Universe bounds are fixed explicitly; changing universe uses the specified enlargement comparisons.
proofSteps: Use tensor product of a finite projective R-endomorphism with a nilpotent A-endomorphism to define the reduced End0(R) action on Nil groups.
Identify NK_j with Nil_(j−1) and transport the action, checking the shift and signs.
The characteristic-series map identifies the Witt completion of End0(R); an element represented by a nilpotent endomorphism of exponent e is annihilated by a sufficiently high filtration ideal.
Extend the action continuously and descend the same operations through Bass’s contraction to all integer degrees.
acceptance: For an NK1 symbol [1−νx] and a Witt characteristic series a(t), substitute νx into the series, so evaluation at x=0 is the identity automorphism.

sources.locator: Theorem 2.3, p.473; Theorem 3.1 and Exercise 3.2, pp.474–475
sources.match: Constructs the continuous big-Witt action through nilpotent endomorphisms and describes a test formula.
