nodes.title: Weibel localization and p-power nilpotent invariance
nodes.statement: For a unital Z[1/p]-algebra A, multiplication by p is an isomorphism on NK_j(A) for every j∈Z; hence the spectrum NK(A)=fib(K(A[x])→K(A)) is uniquely p-divisible and NK(A)^∧p=0. If p^r=0 in A, each NK_j(A) is p-primary torsion. If I⊂A is nilpotent and p^r=0 in A, every relative K_j(A,I) is p-primary torsion, so K(A)→K(A/I) is a rational equivalence.
hypotheses: The unique p-divisibility claim requires p invertible in A.
The torsion and relative nilpotent claims instead require p^r=0 in A.
Universe bounds are fixed explicitly; changing universe uses the specified enlargement comparisons.
proofSteps: For R=Z[1/p], multiplication by p on big Witt vectors is invertible: in the characteristic power-series model it is the pth power map, whose inverse is solved recursively because p is a unit in R.
Apply the continuous action to each NK group; multiplication by p on a spectrum is an equivalence exactly when it is so on every homotopy group.
When p is nilpotent in A, use the finite Witt-filtration annihilator of each element to obtain a p-power annihilator.

For nilpotent I, use the simplicial polynomial/Karoubi–Villamayor comparison: the higher Nil terms are p-primary torsion, and the polynomial-homotopy invariant quotient is nilinvariant. Its relative comparison spectral sequence then makes all relative K groups p-primary; use Bass for nonpositive degrees.
acceptance: For a singular Z[1/p]-algebra NK may be nonzero integrally even though its p-completion is zero.

sources.locator: Corollary 3.3(a),(d), p.475; Corollary 5.4, p.485 and its preceding comparison argument, pp.482–485
sources.match: Proves p-invertibility of NK and p-primary relative K for nilpotent ideals.

nodes.title: ε-enlargement and descent towers
nodes.statement: Let T be a thick subcategory of small stable idempotent-complete C. For finite spectrum F let T_F be the thick closure of T and every F⊗X. For a finite set Σ of primes put T_(ε,Σ)=intersection_F T_F, where F_(q)≠0 for every q∈Σ; put T_ε=union_Σ T_(ε,Σ). An ε-object belongs to 0_ε. A tower is nilpotent if a fixed-length composite of its transition maps is null; it is rapidly convergent if it is in the thick closure of nilpotent and constant towers. An augmented cosimplicial diagram is an ε-nilpotent limit if its cofiber totalization tower lies in the ε-enlargement of the nilpotent towers.
hypotheses: C is small stable idempotent-complete and T is thick.
Σ is finite and F ranges over finite spectra nonzero at each q∈Σ.
Universe bounds are fixed explicitly; changing universe uses the specified enlargement comparisons.
proofSteps: Define thick closures inside C and inside its tower category, using finite-spectrum tensoring.
Prove invariance under exact functors and the Verdier-quotient criterion for ε-enlargement.
Compare finite partial totalizations and their cofiber tower with the augmentation.
acceptance: The ε condition has a uniform finite set of primes; arbitrary pointwise periodic acyclicity is not its definition.

sources.match: Defines ε-enlargements and the towers needed for periodic descent.

nodes.title: Rational transfer forces periodic descent
nodes.statement: In a symmetric monoidal stable idempotent-complete ∞-category C, let R be commutative, A associative, and M an A-module with a map M→R for which π0 Map_C(1,M)⊗Q→π0 Map_C(1,R)⊗Q has the unit of R in its image. Then R lies in the ε-enlargement of the thick tensor ideal generated by A, and CB•aug(A)⊗R is an ε-nilpotent limit. In a presentable stable target, any such diagram satisfies L_n^fX_(−1)≃L_n^fTot(X•)≃Tot(L_n^fX•), and its localized totalization tower is rapidly convergent. The tower conclusion also holds with L_T(i), i≥1, by the same ε argument.
hypotheses: C is stable symmetric monoidal, R commutative, A associative, and M an A-module mapping to R rationally onto its unit.
The totalization conclusion uses a presentable stable target.
Universe bounds are fixed explicitly; changing universe uses the specified enlargement comparisons.
proofSteps: Clear finitely many rational denominators and fix their finite prime set Σ.

In the Verdier quotient by the tensor ideal generated by M and a Σ-nonzero finite spectrum, the image of R has a nilpotent integer unit annihilator. Its rational and mod-q homology vanish at every q; apply May nilpotence to its commutative endomorphism algebra and conclude R=0.
Thus R belongs to the indicated ε-tensor ideal; the thick-ideal cobar argument yields the ε-nilpotent totalization tower.

Finite chromatic localization identifies each ε-enlargement with its original thick subcategory; apply this to towers. Both localization-before-limit and limit-before-localization annihilate the cofiber tower, giving the two separate equivalences.
acceptance: Localization commutes with this totalization by the proven uniform tower property; no general commutation with inverse limits is asserted.

sources.locator: Theorems 4.2–4.4 with proofs, p.19; Proposition 2.23, pp.13–14; Propositions 2.13 and 2.19, pp.11–13

nodes.title: Nonpositive nilpotent invariance
nodes.statement: For a discrete unital ring A and nilpotent two-sided ideal I, K_j(A)→K_j(A/I) is an isomorphism for every j≤0. This is the Bass induction extending K0 nilinvariance, whose owner remains KTheoryLowDegrees Z.1; no positive-degree integral nilinvariance is asserted.
hypotheses: A is discrete unital; I is a nilpotent two-sided ideal; j≤0.
Universe bounds are fixed explicitly; changing universe uses the specified enlargement comparisons.
proofSteps: Use the imported lifting of idempotents/projectives modulo nilpotent ideals to compare K0.
Apply Bass’s polynomial/Laurent fundamental sequence to A and A/I; their extended ideals remain nilpotent.
Induct down all negative degrees and compare the actual quotient-induced maps.
acceptance: For Z/p^r→Fp all negative groups vanish and K0 identifies with Z.

sources.match: Uses the standard extension of K0 nilinvariance to all nonpositive degrees.

nodes.title: Redshift in chromatic graded pieces
nodes.statement: For an E∞-ring R of nonnegative chromatic height and every n≥1, vanishing of the nth graded piece of its p-primary finite chromatic tower is equivalent to vanishing of the (n+1)st graded piece for K(R). The same vanishing equivalence holds for the corresponding ordinary chromatic tower. On p-local R one may also include n=0, with L0=HQ and M0=L0. Globally T0=S[1/p] is not replaced by HQ in this translation.
hypotheses: R is E∞ of nonnegative height and n≥1.
For the n=0 extension, R is p-local.
Universe bounds are fixed explicitly; changing universe uses the specified enlargement comparisons.
proofSteps: Use the commutative-ring initial-interval height theorem and the ring-spectrum comparison of vanishing at T(n) and K(n) for n≥1.

For n≥1 the graded-piece question concerns positive height cutoffs. If ht(R)≥1 use positive-height redshift. If global ht(R)=0, the upper bound makes the (n+1)st piece of K(R) vanish and the nth piece of R already vanishes; no height-zero lower bound is needed.
For n=0 restrict to p-local input to compare S[1/p] with HQ; record the extra restriction rather than changing the global bottom convention.
acceptance: This is a comparison of vanishing, not an equivalence of the two towers or the telescope conjecture.

sources.locator: Interpretation after the Redshift Theorem, p.1014; Lemma 2.3, p.1016
sources.match: Translates the height equality into vanishing of graded chromatic pieces.

sourceIssues.locator: LMMT published introduction, p.1014, Redshift Theorem and its Nullstellensatz discussion; compare Definition 2.1, p.1016, with BSY §9 opening, p.86, Corollary 5.2, p.55, and Theorem 9.11, p.89.
sourceIssues.printed: In our words: the introduction states redshift for every E∞ ring of nonnegative height and describes a characteristic-zero periodic field map in height zero, while its global convention is T0=S[1/p].
sourceIssues.correction: At height zero require R⊗HQ≠0, or state the theorem for p-local input as in BSY §9. Positive-height redshift and the arbitrary-ring T(n)-purity theorem keep their stated scope. KII.6/redshift uses this corrected domain.
sourceIssues.reason: For an odd coefficient prime p, take R=(HF2)^tC2. It is a nonzero E∞ ring of characteristic 2 with an invertible degree-one class, so R[1/p]=R and every positive telescope at p annihilates R: its global height is 0, but it has no unital map to any characteristic-zero field. On perfect R-modules suspension is equivalent to the identity; additivity makes multiplication by 2 zero on K(R). Since 2 is invertible at odd p, all positive p-telescopes annihilate K(R), so its height is at most 0, contradicting the unrestricted global formula 0+1. This is the BSY Remark 9.13 example evaluated at a different prime. BSY explicitly begins §9 with p-local rings.
sourceIssues.known: No published correction was located in the recorded searches on 2026-10-19. BSY §9 already has the p-local convention. The independent review confirms the source-scope error under LMMT’s stated global T0 convention.

review.reason: Independently checked LMMT pp.1014 and 1016 against BSY §9 pp.86–90 and Corollary 5.2 p.55. BSY assumes p-local rings. At an odd coefficient prime the characteristic-two one-periodic E∞ ring of Remark 9.13 survives p-inversion, has no rational part, and has 2-torsion K-theory by additivity; its positive odd-primary telescopes vanish. This disproves the unrestricted global height-zero conclusion and confirms the rational-part correction used by the nodes.
